title: Value-Cost-Latency (VCL) prioritization framework and rollout
creator: Priya Singh
description: Problem: Existing RICE-derived scoring has been useful but misses an explicit, quantitative way to trade off monetary cost and tail/percentile latency impact for production inference workloads. Goal: introduce a pragmatic, repeatable framework that augments RICE/OKR signals with a cost and latency penalty so PMs, Eng, and Platform can prioritize features and infra work in a way that maps to unit economics and SLO risk. Outcome: a VCL (Value-Cost-Latency) score, templates, a calculation spreadsheet, and an automation that tags top candidates in Linear + updates the roadmap leaderboard each cycle.
acceptance_criteria: VCL scoring doc published in Confluence with formula, examples, and guidance
Template spreadsheet (Drive) with example calculations for 10 candidate initiatives
Automation: GitHub action or script that pulls estimate/cost/impact and computes VCL scores into a CSV used by roadmap dashboard
PMs and Eng leads have run the framework on last two cycles of backlog candidates and validated ranking against stakeholder expectations
Console dashboard card (roadmap view) shows VCL score and decomposition (Value, Cost, Latency, Confidence) per initiative

decisions: Use a multiplicative VCL score: VCL = (ValueScore * Confidence) / (CostFactor * EffortPoints) * exp(-LatencyPenalty)
CostFactor: normalized 6-month incremental cost in USD scaled to a 0.1-10 range via log transform to avoid domination by absolute dollars
LatencyPenalty: computed from expected increase in 95th->99th percentile latency (ms) mapped to a 0.0-1.0 penalty; 0 = no material tail impact, 1 = high tail risk requiring infra change
ValueScore: composite of OKR alignment (0.0-1.0), estimated user reach (scaled), and impact band (numeric mapping from Design/PM)
Confidence: mapped from RICE confidence; used as linear multiplier (0.25-1.0)
EffortPoints: use Linear estimate points to keep consistency with planning (1-13)
We will not apply the VCL score as sole arbiter; it's intended to be a consistent signal used alongside qualitative review and stakeholder veto.
example_calculation: Example: Deduped KV cache (infra optimization): ValueScore = 0.6 (OKR alignment=0.9, reach moderate), Confidence=0.8, CostFactor=0.3 (saves $120k over 6 months normalized to 0.3), EffortPoints=5, LatencyPenalty=0.05

Compare: small UX polish: ValueScore=0.4, Confidence=0.7, CostFactor=1.1 (costly external infra), EffortPoints=3, LatencyPenalty=0.0 => VCL = (0.4*0.7)/(1.1*3)*1 = 0.28/3.3 = 0.085. Deduped cache ranks higher by VCL despite lower raw RICE reach because of strong cost savings.
